SWATdoctR: old and updated versions

Source: VERSION-HISTORY.md

These version tags expose the source before the SWAT+ 62 update and the tested updated source in this same repository. They do not replace or rewrite the original Git history.

Snapshot Package version Git tag
Old source baseline 0.1.27 before-swat62-update
Updated development version 0.1.32 swat62-v0.1.32

The old tag points to commit 4b1aee0988e63f9678b23cd6e648f89bce34ef14, the exact upstream source commit used before these edits. It is a source baseline for this update, not a claim that every bundled package dates from three years ago.

Review the differences on GitHub

  1. Open the old-to-updated comparison.
  2. Scroll to the changed files. GitHub marks removed lines red and added lines green.
  3. Open individual files or commits to inspect each change. Where available, select the split view to see old and new code side by side.

The comparison above hides whitespace-only changes, which is especially useful for files with different Windows line endings. The complete comparison includes every change. The commit history shows the incremental updates.

Both tags are fixed snapshots. Future versions should receive new version tags; main remains the current working branch. These are maintained development versions, not releases issued by the original authors.

Main changes

  • Run each verification in a fresh directory and update print and nostress settings by field name.
  • Check executable completion and read complete management and fixed-width HRU outputs.
  • Use the shared annual basin reader so calibration descriptions are not mistaken for plant or management labels.
  • Correct the description of nostress = 2: it disables nutrient stresses while retaining other stresses.
  • Stop report generation when SWAT+ diagnostics contain unresolved plant names, preventing silent agrc substitution.
  • Remove temporary verification runs and the empty .run_verify parent on success or error unless keep_folder = TRUE is explicitly requested.

Tested scope

The updated packages ran the supplied migrated reference model with the Windows Intel SWAT+ revision 62 executable. The supplied verification, discharge calibration/validation, sensitivity, crop and water-yield workflows produced outputs. The final source test run covered all seven package test directories and passed 102 expectations. These results do not establish compatibility for every model, executable or optional process; scientific calibration acceptance has not been achieved.

See COMPATIBILITY.md and the workflow results for the tests and limitations. Model input migration and updating the old project-generation layer are separate from these package source comparisons.
